name: ISM Design System rules
description: Machine-readable rules an LLM or a linter needs and cannot infer from the visual boards. Human-readable versions live beside this file as Markdown. Token names refer to tokens/tokens.json.

hooks.hover: :hover (pointer devices only; never the only cue)
hooks.pressed: :active or .is-pressed – one step darker than hover; no scale, no movement
hooks.disabled: [disabled] or [aria-disabled="true"] – opacity var(--opacity-disabled), no pointer events, not focusable when truly disabled
hooks.loading: [aria-busy="true"] or .is-loading – spinner replaces the leading icon, label stays, width does not change, input blocked
hooks.error: [aria-invalid="true"] or .is-error – --error border and --error-field-bg on fields, plus a text message; never colour alone

rules: Every interactive component implements all seven states, or its spec lists which states do not apply and why.
Focus must be visible on every interactive element and may never be removed with outline:none unless replaced by an equal indicator.
Disabled elements keep their label legible; the 0.45 opacity is the only dimming. Do not also grey the text.
Loading never changes the control's size. Do not hide the label.
Error text sits directly below the field, is linked with aria-describedby, and says what to do next.
Hover must not be required to discover an action; touch has no hover.

button.error: not applicable – errors belong to the form, not the button

choice.error: --error border on the control, message under the group

row.focus: inset ring so it is not clipped

overlay.note: No hover or pressed state on the surface itself; actions inside follow the button rules.

fontFallbacks.note: Inter and Lora have no Ethiopic, Myanmar or Arabic glyphs, so the browser falls through the stack per character. Always set lang on the element so :lang() rules apply.

scripts.status: recommended, native-reader review pending; Urdu is conventionally Nastaliq and needs a font decision

typography: Letter-spacing is 0 for Ethiopic, Myanmar and Arabic-script text; tracking breaks joining and stacking.
No uppercase transform, no italics for Ethiopic, Myanmar and Arabic-script text; use weight or colour for emphasis.
Headings in these scripts use the heading line-height from the table, never the Latin 1.12.
Do not truncate with ellipsis mid-word in Myanmar; allow wrapping.

rtl.mechanism: Set dir="rtl" and lang on <html> (or on the content block). Load ism.rtl.css after ism.css; it is generated from the component CSS with postcss-rtlcss. Use CSS logical properties in new code.
mirror: chevrons that mean next, back, previous or drill-in (› ‹)
drawers (slide from the right in RTL)
doNotMirror: ↗ (it points to an external page, not a direction)
media transport: play, pause, skip, scrub position
phone numbers, verse references, numerals, URLs and email addresses (wrap in dir=ltr / .ism-ltr)

utilities..ism-ltr: isolate an LTR run (numbers, URLs) inside RTL text

rtl.scripture: Scripture text keeps the reading direction of its language. Verse numbers stay Latin or Arabic-Indic per language convention; see voice rules.

breakpoints.note: Mobile-first. ≤767 is mobile, 768–1023 tablet, ≥1024 desktop. ≤480 compact tightens padding and stacks button groups.

container.note: .wrap = width 100%, max --container-max (1200), side padding --gutter (24). .narrow = 760. Full-bleed frames cap at --frame-max (1280).

grid.note: The shipped CSS uses flex and CSS grid inside .wrap rather than a fixed column system. When a 12-column grid is needed use repeat(12,1fr) with gap var(--gutter); spans collapse to full width at ≤767.

layout.spacing: 4px base. Use --space-1…--space-10 only (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128). No other values.

zIndex.rule: Use the tokens. Values 3–9 may be used for local layering inside one component only. Never exceed --z-skip.

rules: Cards at rest use card elevation; hover on interactive cards raises to lift.
Anything floating over content (menu, sheet, modal, toast) uses overlay.
Dark surfaces use a border (--border-hairline-dark) instead of shadow.
Color, border and opacity changes: fast, ease-standard.
Drawers, sheets, menus: drawer duration, ease-drawer.
Entrance of page content: enter duration, ease-rise, 20px translate max.
Spinners are linear. Pulse is for the live indicator only.
Honour prefers-reduced-motion: remove translate and scale, keep opacity fades under 150ms, slow spinners.
Never animate layout properties (width, height, top, left) on large areas; animate transform and opacity.

sectionRhythm.note: Classes .sec and .sec-sm. Vertical padding between page sections; use these classes, not ad-hoc padding.

glyphs.meaning: opens something on this page: menu, dropdown, accordion, select, language switcher
goes to another page or another site (new context). The only glyph for external or off-page navigation.
drills into a deeper screen or level (lists in the app, breadcrumbs separator, row affordance)
primary continue in a flow (one per group, on the primary button only)
add or expand a disclosure that adds content (accordion item uses +/−)
dismiss or clear. Always a button with an accessible name.

rules: Links inside body copy are underlined; links in navigation are not, but gain an underline or colour change on hover and a visible focus ring.
Link colour is --horizon-blue on light, --blue-on-dark on dark. Hover is --horizon-blue-dim. Visited links are not restyled.
A link that leaves the site or opens in a new tab shows ↗ and uses target="_blank" rel="noopener"; say so to assistive tech with a visually-hidden "(opens in a new tab)".
Buttons do things, links go places. A control that changes state or submits is a <button>; a control that navigates is an <a>.
Icons are 1.8px stroke, round caps and joins, currentColor, on a 24px grid. Sizes: 16, 20, 24 (--icon-sm, --icon-md, --icon-lg). Do not mix filled and outline in one group.
Decorative icons: aria-hidden="true". Meaningful icons without text: an accessible name on the control, not the svg.
Counts and notification dots are blue. Red is for errors only. The live/on-air dot is --live and used only for on-air.
One Horizon Blue primary per group of actions; everything else is secondary or ghost.

minimums.focusRing: 2px solid --horizon-blue, 2px offset, plus --shadow-focus; on --horizon-blue backgrounds use white; on dark use --blue-on-dark
minimums.textResize: Works at 200% zoom without loss of content; use rem or px in tokens with no fixed-height text containers.

contrastPairs.use: links and ghost buttons on cards
focus ring and UI strokes on black; NOT for text (4.30)
large text or UI on blue tint only (4.43)

forbidden: --horizon-blue as text colour on black or charcoal (use --blue-on-dark)
Colour as the only signal of state, error or meaning

alt: Informative image: alt describes the content and purpose in one sentence, in the page language, no "image of".
Decorative image or pattern: alt="" (and role="presentation" on svg).
Logo as link: alt is the link purpose ("International Scripture Ministries home"), not the logo's appearance.
Functional image (QR code): alt says what it does and what it encodes, and the URL is also given as text.
Photos of people: describe what they are doing, never guess ethnicity, nationality or age.
Text in images is avoided; if unavoidable, the alt carries the exact text.

semantics: Use native elements first: button, a, input, select, details/summary, dialog, nav, main, header, footer.
One h1 per page; headings do not skip levels.
Landmarks are labelled when more than one of a kind exists (nav aria-label).
Modals trap focus, restore focus on close, close on Esc, and label with aria-labelledby.
Toasts use role=status (polite) for success and info and role=alert only for errors.
Form fields have a visible label, an id/for pair, aria-describedby for hint and error, and aria-invalid on error.
Language changes inside a page carry a lang attribute.
Provide a skip link as the first focusable element.
Audio and video: captions or transcript, keyboard-operable controls, no autoplay with sound.

rules: Sentence case everywhere: headings, buttons, labels, menu items. Proper nouns keep their capitals.
No exclamation marks. No emoji. No all-caps except the eyebrow style, which is rendered by CSS not typed.
Write for translation: short sentences, no idioms, no wordplay, no culture-specific metaphors.
Say "you" and "we". Avoid passive voice.
Numbers: numerals for counts (12 languages), spell out one only in running prose.

buttons.rule: Verb first, 1–3 words, says what happens next.
buttons.primaryWithArrow: → only on the primary "continue" button of a flow.

errors.tone: Calm, specific, no blame, no jokes. Say what happened and what to do.

examples.good: Enter an email address like name@example.com.
We couldn't save your changes. Check your connection and try again.
We can't find that page. Go to the home page or search for what you need.

rules: Never use red text alone; include an icon or the word "Error".
Do not clear what the user typed.
Do not say "please" more than once in a view.

voice.emptyStates: Say what will appear here and how to get started. One action.

scripture.reference: Book chapter:verse, with a non-breaking space: John 3:16 · 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 (en dash for ranges). Use the book names of the reader's language and tradition.
scripture.quotation: Scripture text is set in Lora, never edited, never ellipsised without marking, and always followed by its reference and the translation abbreviation (e.g. NIV, RVR60, or the language's translation name).
scripture.naming: Say "Scripture", "the Bible" or "God's Word" consistently with how the translation names itself. Capitalise God, Lord (when YHWH) and pronouns per translation convention; do not decide this in UI code.
scripture.verseNumbers: Verse numbers are small, superscript-style, --gray-600, not selectable in copy by default.
scripture.attribution: Always show translation and copyright line where required by the licence.
neverDo: Paraphrase scripture in UI copy and present it as a quote
Use scripture as decoration without its reference
Change verse text for fit; shorten the passage instead

orgName.rule: Write "dot.Bible" with a capital B. Write "ISM" in capitals. Do not abbreviate the organisation in the first mention.

buildingRules: One Horizon Blue primary action per group.
Inter for UI (h1 weight 700, other headings 600); Lora for scripture and quotes only.
Logos are black ink; on dark backgrounds invert with filter: brightness(0) invert(1). Never recolour, rotate or stretch a logo; keep clear space of the dot height.
Use tokens, never raw hex, px radius, shadows or z-index values.
Cards: white on off-white, radius --radius-lg (20), --shadow-card-light, 24px padding; no card inside a card.
Pills (--radius-pill) are for buttons, chips and badges; inputs use --radius-md (12) and are at least 48px high.
Use only the gradient tokens (--gradient-signature, -line, -marker, -signature-soft and the stop colours); --gradient-signature is for hero accents and the brand bar, never behind text.
Tap targets are at least 44px on every platform.
